notes: Use auto-rickshaws and Uber in Jaipur; hire a car by the day for the forts (about 2,500 INR). The composite ticket (1,500 INR for foreigners) covers 8 monuments over 2 days.
October to March is the best season (15-28°C). January brings the Kite Festival, and March brings Holi (colourful and chaotic).
Try dal baati churma, pyaz kachori, ghewar and lassi. There is no meat or alcohol in Pushkar. Tip 10%.
Monument entry costs foreigners 200-1,000 INR. Amber is cool and empty at 08:00; take a jeep rather than an elephant.
Book the Ranthambore safari online 3 months ahead (tiger zones 1-5). Staying overnight isn't essential for the safari, but it's more comfortable.
Haggling: start at a third of the first price. Buy block-printed fabric from the makers in Sanganer.

stops.name: Hawa Mahal
stops.tips: The Palace of Winds has 953 windows. Morning light hits the facade, so shoot it from the café opposite (Wind View).

stops.name: City Palace Jaipur
stops.tips: The maharaja's palace, with the Four Seasons gates in the Pritam Niwas courtyard, and a museum.

stops.name: Jantar Mantar Jaipur
stops.tips: A giant stone observatory with a 27 m sundial. UNESCO listed.

stops.name: Laxmi Misthan Bhandar
stops.tips: On Johari Bazaar since 1727. Try dal baati churma, ghewar and pyaz kachori.

stops.name: Johari Bazaar
stops.tips: Jewellery and block-printed fabric. Haggle, and note the shops are shaded in the midday heat.

backups.name: Rawat Misthan Bhandar
backups.tips: Pyaz kachori, a street food favourite.

backups.name: Albert Hall Museum
backups.tips: An Indo-Saracenic museum, air-conditioned and lit up at night.

stops.name: Amber Fort
stops.tips: A Rajput hilltop fort with the Sheesh Mahal mirror palace. Take a jeep rather than an elephant, and go at the 08:00 opening while it's cool.

stops.name: Panna Meena ka Kund
stops.tips: A stepwell below Amber, great for symmetrical photos.

stops.name: Jaigarh Fort
stops.tips: Home to Jaivana, the world's largest wheeled cannon, above Amber.

stops.name: 1135 AD Amber Fort Restaurant
stops.tips: A royal thali served on silver plates inside the fort.

stops.name: Nahargarh Fort
stops.tips: A fort overlooking the city. Watch the sunset and the Pink City lights from Padao café.

backups.name: Samode Haveli Restaurant
backups.tips: Lunch in a haveli, instead of the fort.

backups.name: Jal Mahal
backups.tips: A palace in the middle of a lake, viewed from outside at sunset, instead of Nahargarh.

stops.name: Galtaji Monkey Temple
stops.tips: Sacred pools and monkeys in a valley. Cool in the morning; cameras cost 200 INR.

stops.name: Birla Mandir Jaipur
stops.tips: A white marble Lakshmi Narayan temple.

stops.name: Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing
stops.tips: A block-printing museum in Amber, with a workshop demonstration.

stops.name: Anokhi Cafe Jaipur
stops.tips: An organic café with a block-print shop downstairs.

stops.name: Sanganer Block Printing Workshops
stops.tips: Jaipur's printing village, with fabric and paper factories. Buy direct from the makers.

backups.name: Tapri Central Jaipur
backups.tips: A rooftop tea house serving chai and bun maska.

backups.name: Patrika Gate
backups.tips: A brightly painted gate at Jawahar Circle, instead of Sanganer.

stops.name: Pushkar Lake Ghats
stops.tips: 2.5 hours from Jaipur. A sacred lake with 52 ghats; go barefoot and beware of flower sellers.

stops.name: Brahma Temple Pushkar
stops.tips: One of the world's few Brahma temples, in blue and white.

stops.name: Pushkar Bazaar
stops.tips: A hippie market selling leather, silver and music.

stops.name: Sunset Cafe Pushkar
stops.tips: A lakeside café. It's vegetarian (no meat or alcohol in Pushkar); try the falafel.

stops.name: Savitri Temple Ropeway
stops.tips: Take the cable car to the hilltop temple for lake and desert views at sunset. A camel safari is optional.

backups.name: Pushkar Camel Safari
backups.tips: A camel ride in the dunes at sunset, instead of the temple.

stops.name: Ranthambore National Park Safari
stops.tips: 3.5 hours from Jaipur (ideally stay a night). Take a morning jeep safari in tiger zones 1-5; book online 3 months ahead.

stops.name: Ranthambore Fort
stops.tips: A 10th-century fort inside the park, with a Ganesh temple and lake views.

stops.name: Ranthambore Dhaba Lunch
stops.tips: A dhaba in Sawai Madhopur serving dal and roti.

stops.name: Dastkar Ranthambore
stops.tips: Handicrafts from a women's cooperative, including tiger-print textiles.

backups.name: Ranthambore Afternoon Safari
backups.tips: A second chance to spot tigers, instead of shopping.

backups.name: Sawai Madhopur Station Canteen
backups.tips: A meal at the railway station.

stops.name: Govind Dev Ji Temple
stops.tips: A Krishna temple in the City Palace gardens. The morning aarti (prayer ritual) is crowded and lively.

stops.name: Bapu Bazaar
stops.tips: Jaipur's market for textiles and mojari (leather slippers). Haggle.

stops.name: Masala Chowk
stops.tips: An open-air local food court in Ram Niwas Garden, serving pani puri and pav bhaji.

stops.name: Hawa Mahal Rooftop Cafés
stops.tips: Sunset tea with a view of Hawa Mahal from the Tattoo Cafe rooftop.

stops.name: Chokhi Dhani
stops.tips: A Rajasthani village-themed evening with puppets, camels and unlimited dal baati (20 km from the city).

backups.name: Peacock Rooftop Pearl Palace
backups.tips: A rooftop restaurant, instead of the village park.

backups.name: Jawahar Kala Kendra
backups.tips: Correa's arts centre with exhibitions, instead of the market.

days.theme: Block prints and a light farewell

stops.name: Rambagh Palace Gardens
stops.tips: The gardens of the palace hotel, with peacocks. Have breakfast or tea (expensive).

stops.name: Anokhi Café Jaipur
stops.tips: An organic café and block-print shop for a farewell breakfast.

stops.name: Jaipur Modern
stops.tips: Modern Rajasthani design souvenirs.

stops.name: Jaipur Airport Road
stops.tips: The airport is 30 minutes away. Farewell.

backups.name: Sahu Chai Wala
backups.tips: Legendary street tea on Chaura Rasta. Have a farewell chai.

backups.name: Ram Niwas Garden
backups.tips: The garden around Albert Hall, instead of the shop.
